_comment: The ruler ids. Every HAL accuracy number must be stated as 'F1 = x on <corpus>@<hash> at N families'. tests/corpus-files.test.ts re-derives these hashes from the files and fails if they move, so a corpus edit cannot land silently — change a label, this file must change in the same commit.
retired_reason: BUS S60: the holdout splits (rigorous-v1 99, canary-v1 15) and their copies have been public in git since July 2026, and a source_id field gives the label away on 190 of 337 rigorous rows, so they are training, regression and practice sets now, never a holdout. Every score on them carries holdout: retired-public. The measurement holdout is private: eval/holdout/README.md.

corpora.name: rigorous-v1
corpora.dropped_reason: source_url was a label annotation ('false stereotype', 'indexical', 'subjective'), not an absolute URL. Dropped rather than patched with a plausible link — the provenance gate exists precisely to stop that.

corpora.name: hal-v1-frozen
corpora.selection: every rigorous-v1@596f10de18d0 row whose notes name a published third-party benchmark (source=halueval|fever|truthfulqa), byte-identical to its rigorous-v1 line. Nothing relabelled, nothing added.
corpora.provenance: 284/284 rows (100%) carry source dataset + source_id + absolute source_url, assigned mechanically by scripts/eval/build-rigorous-corpus.py (seed 42) from the upstream files. Upstream content was NOT re-fetched and re-matched in this change.

excluded.reason: claims written in-repo (eval/canary, commit 9ccc91a1) with a Wikipedia citation: no third-party dataset and no item id, label assigned by us. Rule 19: self-authored, not provenanced.
already dropped from rigorous-v1 (see its dropped_reason).

mutable and unhashed (relabels recorded in notes), duplicate texts, and the population the validation runs and threshold work were taken on. Most rows are swarm-written with no source URL; one benchmark import has no item ids. The id-carrying benchmark imports could seed a separate, separately-hashed corpus; they are not merged into this ruler.

corpora.holdout: NONE. Every row is public in git (retired as a holdout 2026-10-07), and the rigorous-v1 holdout split was used to fit reports/hal-eval/hal-calibrator-rigorous-v1.json (fittedOn 99). The split field is kept from rigorous-v1 for regression only: a score on any split of this corpus is holdout: retired-public, never a holdout score.

_open_decision: answer_mode is 'claim-as-answer' for both: prompt is a fixed verification instruction, candidate_answer is the claim. 190 of the 337 rigorous rows were built 'qa->statement' and could have their Q/A recovered instead, but the other 197 have no question to recover — mixing both inside one corpus would put two different measurements under one F1, which is the ruler-mixing this rack exists to end. Use --answer-mode recover-qa only to build a SEPARATE, separately-named, separately-hashed corpus. Not ratified by Sean.
